Procedure
Step 1 Label three test-tubes A, B and C.
Step 2 Use a syringe to add 5 cm of 4% enzyme solution to test-tube A.
Step 3 Use a clean syringe to add 5 cm of 2% enzyme solution to test-tube B.
Step 4 Use a clean syringe to add 5 cm of 1% enzyme solution to test-tube C.
Step 5 Use a clean syringe to add 2 cm of milk to test-tube A.
Step 6 Use a clean glass stirring rod to mix the contents of test-tube A.
Step 7 Start the stop-watch.
Step 8 Measure the time it takes for the milk in test-tube A to become clear.

protein.
Milk contains a protein that makes it look white (opaque).
When the protein is broken down, the milk becomes clear.

appear changes.

Method 1
Plan an investigation to find out if the material from which a spring is made affects the extension of
the spring when it is stretched by a load.
You are provided with:
• springs made from aluminium, steel, iron and nickel
• a set of 100 g masses, together with a hanger
• boss, stand and clamp.
You may use any other common laboratory apparatus.
You are not required to do this investigation.
In your plan include:
• any other apparatus needed
• a brief description of the method, including what you will measure and how you will make
sure your measurements are accurate
• the variables you will control
• a results table to record your measurements (you are not required to enter any readings in
the table)
• how you will process your results to draw a conclusion.
You may include a labelled diagram if you wish.
